CYCLEREVIEW_ICLR2024.argument: This paper proposes a benchmark for MLLMs on low-level visual perception and understanding.
The authors propose three abilities: perception, description, and assessment.

To evaluate the perception ability, the authors construct the LLVisionQA dataset, which consists of 2,990 diverse-sourced images, each equipped with a human-asked question focusing on its low-level attributes.
To examine the description ability of MLLMs on low-level information, the authors propose the LLDescribe dataset consisting of long expert-labelled golden low-level text descriptions on 499 images.

To measure their visual quality assessment ability to align with human opinion scores, the authors design a softmax-based strategy that enables MLLMs to predict quantifiable quality scores, and evaluate them on various existing image quality assessment (IQA) datasets.
The paper is well-written and easy to follow.
The proposed benchmark is comprehensive and covers three abilities: perception, description, and assessment.
The proposed softmax-based strategy for predicting quantifiable quality scores is effective.
The paper does not provide a clear definition of low-level visual perception and understanding.
It is not clear what are the specific tasks that the benchmark is designed for.
The paper does not provide a comprehensive analysis of the results.
For example, how do the results compare to human performance?
What are the limitations of the benchmark?
The paper does not provide a clear description of the experimental setup, including the evaluation metrics and the evaluation protocol.
The paper does not provide a clear description of the results, including the performance of the MLLMs on the benchmark and the comparison to human performance.
